column2: Changed: 15 min cooldown, 60% less damage for 12 sec (Classic was 30 min, 75% for 10 sec). It no longer shares a cooldown with Retaliation and Recklessness: each has its own timer in the beta files, and Blizzard says so in its Class Highlights video (1:14). Two readers flagged it first.
Energy comes back 1 point every 0.1 sec, 10 a second. Same rate as Classic, but no tick to wait for. From the beta's Energy tooltip, and Blizzard's Class Highlights video (3:41).

Gives the Paladin a chance to deal additional Holy damage equal to 70% of normal weapon damage. Only one Seal can be active on the Paladin at any one time. Lasts 30 sec. Unleashing this Seal's energy will judge an enemy, instantly causing 68 to 73 Holy damage, 137 to 145 if the target is stunned or incapacitated.

Lasting totems last 5 min now. Most were 2 min in Classic, and Healing Stream and Mana Spring were 1 min. Disease Cleansing Totem still lasts 2 min in the beta. Searing (30 sec), Magma (20), Stoneclaw (15), Earthbind and Grounding (45) and Mana Tide (12) keep their short timers. From the beta files; Blizzard's Class Highlights video (3:00) says five minutes.
New: each drops up to four totems from its own Totem Bar set in one 3 sec cast. Call of the Elements at 20, Call of the Ancestors at 30, Call of the Spirits at 40, so three saved sets by 40.
Rage and Energy, the way they come in now

Rage comes from taking damage and from your melee swings. Slower weapons give more Rage per swing, so it comes in at a steady rate instead of scaling with how hard you hit. Out of combat you lose 1.25 Rage a second (75 a minute). From the beta's Rage tooltip, and Blizzard's Class Highlights video (0:23).

Shaman: Stormstrike comes at 25, not 40
The Mage guide: the count of what changed, and the video chapter by chapter

The Shaman spellbook said Stormstrike is learned at level 40. That is the level the game files give the spell itself, left over from Classic, where it was the 31-point talent. In Forever the talent sits in row 4 of Enhancement, which opens at 15 points, so a Shaman can have it at 25. The book says 25 now, and the tooltip says where the 40 came from. The same rule caught four more talent spells that moved down a row or two: Mana Tide Totem (25, not 40), Vampiric Embrace (25, not 30), Counterattack (25, not 30) and Soul Link (30, not 40). Thanks to u/HOUDINl.
The site got more fun to use

When a beta build moves the trees, one email says what moved: the count, the class icons with their numbers, and your own classes first with their biggest changes, the way this panel shows it. Then a link to the rest. Tick the news box on Back to Class and leave an address; you confirm with one click, and the same link in every message stops it. A few times a month at most, and never on a quiet week.

You know Classic. The new Mage guide at talentsforever.com/mage/changes is only what is different now, told the way the video tells it: what is new, the trees before and after, Frost, Fire and Arcane, your damage and your gear, the races that can be a Mage, and what people are building. Each chapter has its part of the video right there, and every number comes from the same beta data the calculator runs on. Mage is first. If you would like a note when your class is up, tick it on Back to Class and leave an email: one message when its guide is ready, with the link, then nothing.
